turns.prompt_text: I have many Google Keep notes, and I would like to organize them. But first, I would like to download them or move them onto my Google Drive.
turns.response_html:
To export your Google Keep notes or move them to Google Drive, you have two primary options depending on how you want to use the files afterward. Google Keep does not have a direct "Move to Drive" button for all notes at once inside the mobile app, but you can do it easily via a web browser or use Google Takeout for a bulk download.

Here are the best methods to handle this.

Option 1: Copy to Google Docs (Best for Drive)

This method converts your notes into Google Docs, which are automatically saved in your Google Drive. This is ideal if you want to edit and organize the text later.

For a Single Note or Few Notes:

  1. Open Google Keep.
  2. Click the three-dot menu on the note you want to move.
  3. Select Copy to Google Docs.
  4. A notification will appear saying "Saving to Google Docs." Click Open Doc to view it immediately in Drive.

For All (or Many) Notes at Once (Web Browser Only):

  1. Go to keep.google.com on your computer.
  2. Hover over the first note you want to select and click the checkmark in the top left corner of the note.
  3. Scroll down to the last note. Hold Shift on your keyboard and click the last note to select everything in between. (Or click Ctrl + A / Cmd + A to select all loaded notes).
  4. Click the three-dot menu in the top right of the screen.
  5. Select Copy to Google Docs.
  6. This will create a batch of Google Docs in your Drive containing your notes.

Option 2: Google Takeout (Best for Downloading)

If you want to download a backup of all your notes to your computer (offline), use Google Takeout.

  1. Go to takeout.google.com.
  2. Click Deselect all (so you don't download your entire Google account history).
  3. Scroll down and check the box next to Keep.
  4. Scroll to the bottom and click Next step.
  5. Choose your file type (usually .zip) and delivery method (e.g., "Send download link via email").
  6. Click Create export.
  7. Google will email you a link to download a Zip file containing your notes (usually in HTML or JSON format).

Summary of Differences

FeatureCopy to Google DocsGoogle Takeout
DestinationGoogle DriveYour Computer (Hard Drive)
FormatEditable DocumentHTML / JSON
Best ForEditing & OrganizingArchiving & Backups
